newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW -- UK industrial output, PMI services.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- UK industrial output, PMI services.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK data showing June manufacturing output rose 0.4 percent m/m and 1.2 percent y/y, while the July PMI services survey showed a slight moderation in the recent strong pace of growth:
"The important thing is to look at the trend and they (the data) are still really pretty weak, below trend growth, both in manufacturing and in industrial production.
"This (weakness in three-month on three-month output data) contrasts with the initial estimates we've had of GDP... that growth is not coming from manufacturing, it's coming from services."

"The rebound in manufacturing demonstrates that conditions in the sector aren't as dire as the May decline suggested. With sterling's current strength, I don't think manufacturers will have much to cheer about. On the PMI data, the fall in the business activity index suggests that the service sector may not be as strong as we thought a couple of months ago. Nevertheless, growth in the economy remains above trend."

"It's encouraging that manufacturing is up in the month, but the fact that it was only up partially doesn't come near to making up for last month's fall. The general trend doesn't show any growth at all in second quarter of the year for the manufacturing industry. Where we go from here is crucial depending on the outlook for the domestic economy. That's where the PMI survey comes into play -- that's still showing strong growth although slightly slower than in previous months. The overall picture of strong service sector and weak manufacturing has not changed at all."

"The UK data are firm enough to support speculation about a rate hike on Thursday. Although manufacturing output rebounded a modest 0.4 percent in June, the CIPS survey shows that the more important services sector is still growing very strongly.

"The overall diffusion index edged a touch softer in July, but at 62.1 percent is still indicative of robust growth. Moreover, the input price index edged up to 57.7 percent, well above the key 50 percent mark, and potentially indicative of some acceleration in wages.
"Prices charged came in at 52.1 percent, which probably reflects ongoing competitive conditions."
